The target expressly requires simplifying the polynomial before substitution, rather than just direct evaluation.
The difference-of-squares identity can be justified by dissection, and the criteria ask to identify/use the structure rather than derive it by termwise multiplication.
set.scope: Justifying the difference of squares identity

set.reason: The source expressly permits an area interpretation of the perfect-square identity; polynomial multiplication is one derivation, not the only route to the stated formula-use criteria.

Contrasting the independent identities usefully prevents confusing a square of a sum with a product of a sum and difference. No learning order is necessary, but that misconception-prevention role supports preparation rather than mere thematic association.
set.scope: Contrasting two independent identities to avoid an omitted middle term

set.reason: A square-area dissection explains the middle term, while algebraic binomial expansion is another valid explanation. The area formula is helpful preparation, not universal necessity.
This factoring method is the difference-of-squares identity read from right to left; its structure is the operation's basis.
